errors.english: they are not marked as thoroughly established
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'have not come about' denotes the unproduced thoroughly established (pariniṣpanna) characteristic, i.e. it identifies them with that nature rather than denying it.

note: A careful, close rendering of Haribhadra-type commentary; only the gloss on the pariniṣpanna characteristic is inverted, and the bam po marker is replaced by a heading.

errors.english: The phrase (only a cessation) Tibetan: pa tsam zad pa
errors.why: With the previous side this is ནོར་པ་ཙམ་ཟད་པ་ཡིན, 'is nothing but an error'; ཙམ་ཟད་ means 'merely', not 'cessation'.

fix.find: The phrase (only a cessation) Tibetan: pa tsam zad pa
fix.replace: The phrase "[the rope too] is merely an error"

errors.english: refers to the lack of stainless primordial wisdom
errors.why: The instrumental says 'not known' means not known by uncontaminated wisdom (the agent of knowing), not an absence of that wisdom.

note: Mostly sound on Sthiramati's argument, but two glosses on the root-verse words are misconstrued.

errors.english: Harmful actions toward the Three Jewels should be eliminated
errors.why: The patient is persons: 'those who harm the Three Jewels are to be killed', part of the antinomian samaya formula; the English converts them into actions.

note: A faithful rendering of the initiation verses; the one samaya line is softened from persons to actions.

errors.english: through the stages of the four results and the paths of the four results
errors.why: The eight are the paths (approachers) to the four fruits and the fruits (abiders) of the four paths.

fix.find: through the stages of the four results and the paths of the four results
fix.replace: by way of the paths to the four results and the results of the four paths

note: Accurate on the qualities of Buddha, Dharma and Saṅgha; the closing eightfold division is garbled, and unmarked inline glosses are added throughout.

errors.english: at the heart of the bird
errors.why: With the previous side this is བསྒྲུབ་བྱའི་སྙིང་གར, 'at the heart of the target of the rite (sādhya)', not a bird.

fix.find: at the heart of the bird
fix.replace: at the heart of the person who is the target of the rite

errors.why: དབབ་པ is the rite of causing descent/possession (āveśa), as the text itself later explains with 'descent', not summoning.

errors.english: Killing refers to using a chain of (vajra) hooks
errors.why: The item is binding (འཆིང་བ, as the later application 'bound by the vajra-chain messenger' shows); 'killing' follows a scribal slip.

errors.english: By praising the tip of its central prong from one's own heart
errors.why: The action is projecting/moving the central prong out from one's heart (བསྟོད read as བསྐྱོད/བཏོན); 'praising' makes no sense in the ritual.

note: Follows the ritual sequence but several key ritual actions are misread, starting with the bird.

errors.why: The passage, with Vajrapāṇi addressing Brahmā and the gods, is not the Hevajra; 'king of tantras' here is the root text being commented on.

errors.english: I shall pay homage to the Blessed One Vajrapani
errors.why: The gods say 'we shall regard [this tantra] as being the Blessed Vajrapāṇi' (and likewise 'regard it as a stūpa'); འཚལ་བར་བགྱི is 'regard', and ལགས་པར 'as being' is lost.

note: The exhortation passage is rendered well; the 'we shall regard it as' formula is turned into homage, and the gloss misidentifies the tantra.
A faithful rendering of the bhūmi-purification list and the Buddha-field passage.

errors.why: Nāgārjuna's verse says the Sambhogakāya's own splendour transcends the world and is inconceivable; 'worldly' inverts it.

fix.replace: whose own splendour transcends the world and is inconceivable

note: The commentary and the Śakra analogy are rendered well, but the quoted verse inverts its key epithet.
A faithful rendering of the transition to the practice chapter and the five objects of training.
A faithful rendering of the ten perfections and the emptiness/non-nihilism argument.
